A_target.statement: The [[Definition:Quotient Ring|quotient ring]] $\R \sqbrk x / \ideal {x^2 + 1}$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] isomorphic to $\C$.

B_source.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $f \in K \sqbrk x$.
Then $K \sqbrk x / \ideal f$ is a field {{iff}} $f$ is [[Definition:Irreducible Polynomial|irreducible]] over $K$.

object_map.reformulation: Specialize the irreducible-quotient construction to x^2 + 1 over the reals.

validity_conditions: x^2 + 1 is irreducible over R since it has degree 2 and no real root.
The division algorithm gives each class a unique representative of degree at most 1.
proof_plan:
$x^2 + 1 > 0$ on $\R$, so it has no real root.
Being of degree $2$, it is [[Definition:Irreducible Polynomial|irreducible]] over $\R$.
By the source result, $\R \sqbrk x / \ideal {x^2 + 1}$ is a field.
By division by $x^2 + 1$, each class has a unique representative $a + b x$, and $x^2 \equiv -1$.
